newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-FRENCH MUSKETEERS FAIL TO DETHRONE CHINESE.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-FRENCH MUSKETEERS FAIL TO DETHRONE CHINESE.

text.p: The three French musketeers of table tennis made a brave but futile attempt to dethrone China at the world championships on Wednesday when the Chinese won the men's team title for the 12th time.

The final was much closer than expected with the Asian powerhouses retaining the crown 3-1. The victory followed on Tuesday's success in the women's event -- the ninth time China have completed the team double.
China's next target is to repeat their 1995 clean sweep of all seven titles. But that is a tall target.
The Chinese trio for the men's team final was formidable -- world champoion Kong Linghui, Olympic gold medallist Liu Guoliang and Olympic silver medalist Wang Tao.
But cracks are starting to appear in the Chinese wall of invulnerability.

On Wednesday it was Liu's turn to experience his first defeat of the championships, losing 21-17 21-16 21-10 to the left-hander Patrick Chilla, who exposed the penholder's weakness down the backhand wing.

World champion Kong, already beaten twice here, was taken the full distance by 1993 titleholder Jean-Philippe Gatien, the talented left-hander, who won the first game before succumbing 18-21 21-16 21-17.
The 20-year-old Kong, admitting he was very nervous playing in his first championship team final, struggled to find his rhythm before finally subduing Gatien with some fierce counter-hitting.
But the highlight of the final was the third match on table between Wang, the 28-year-old team veteran, and Damien Eloi.
Wang's stunning hitting power swept him to a 21-10 victory in the first game and he looked in complete command when he led 20-16 in the second.
But Eloi battled back bravely, saving 10 match points before finally losing 31-29 when he could not control a fierce Wang forehand drive.
The crowd were held spellbound as the left-handed Wang chased the elusive winning point only to be foiled by Eloi.

"It is the first time I have ever experienced a 31-29 score," Wang said later. "Certainly I didn't expect anything like that when I led 20-16. I was just too eager to finish it off," added Wang who emerged as the only undefeated Chinese team player.
Wang's win made it 2-1 in China's favour and Liu grabbed the chance to make up for his earlier lapses by beating Gatien 21-19 21-14 to clinch yet another Chinese triumph.
Chinese team coach Cai Zenhua was full of praise for his team, Wang in particular.
"His win was the key to the whole match," Cai said. "We prepared well and our win against Sweden in the quarter-finals gave us confidence. We then felt strong enough for Korea and France."
